title: status.schema.json verdict-field cap and phase-list enforcement (test-status-schema-contract.sh)
content: Issue #34 (folded in #42, PR #51); the KNOWN OPEN GAP this entry used to carry (the '0-setup' Lane 1/Lane 2 population mismatch) was CLOSED by #53 (merged to main as 055038e, PR #79) -- see the resolution paragraph below before relying on anything in the historical #34 material. PROVENANCE: the #34 reasoning below was surveyed and reviewed at d8686bc19d317d89d1ec29b8d2cf13c196bb30ff (the commit the Phase 4 panel actually reviewed); PR #51 was then rebase-merged after two further rounds (a nit round closing two demonstrated AC10 escapes and adding a pipeline.md writer rule, and a post-CI fix re-founding the events/flags discrimination on a crafted tree), which rewrote every SHA -- what actually shipped on main for #34 is 0d0b8d5 (range 1035473..0d0b8d5), released in 0.23.0 as c064b3b. Keep both SHAs: d8686bc predates the events/flags discrimination fix and diffing there shows that cell still broken; use 0d0b8d5 for the #34 shipped state, 055038e for current. Added plugins/pipeline/tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh (67 assertions) as the ONLY thing that makes status.schema.json's constraints load-bearing rather than decorative -- see the architecture--status-schema-json-consumers.json entry for why nothing else reads or validates this file. What it does: (1) events[].verdict and flags[].verdict both carry maxLength:32 (raised from unbounded; ruled at 1.78x the 18-char longest value in the declared verdict enum union across status/peer-review/review schemas, deliberately far below flags[].summary's existing 140 cap, which the panel called a comment-that-throws rather than a control). (2) A vacuity-controlled corpus walk over every committed .pipeline/*/status.json (derived floor, never pinned to a fixed count -- floor is max(git-index count, on-disk count) with a >=1 assertion plus explicit crafted-tree cells for zero-records, unparseable JSON, and events-as-object, so an empty corpus cannot pass by omission) asserts every committed verdict string is <= the cap, reading the cap FROM the schema rather than a copied literal (proven by mutation: change only the schema's maxLength and the check's verdict moves). (3) The current_phase description's example phase list is corrected against commands/pipeline.md by SET EQUALITY in both directions (not substring grep -- voice-lint.mjs's own earlier phase table failed exactly that way), with halted-error deliberately kept even though pipeline.md never writes it, because gate-phase-entry.mjs blesses it by name (re-derive with `git grep -n 'phase === "halted-error"' -- plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`) and the schema's own pattern alternates it as a shape. NON-ZERO CONTROL ON RECORD (permanent, not one-shot): temporarily setting the cap to 17 must turn AC3 red and must NAME .pipeline/17/status.json's flags[] entry 'APPROVE_WITH_NOTES' (18 chars) as the violator; a FIRES cell may rest on the live corpus because it only grows, a SILENCE cell may not because any added record can break it -- so SILENCE cells were moved onto crafted trees while the FIRES cell stayed anchored to the live corpus. Watch this cap: at #53's own Phase 5 checkpoint the orchestrator's `SCOPE_DRIFT_DECLARED` (20 chars) and `SHARD_NONCONFORMANT` (19 chars) prose verdicts briefly exceeded every prior corpus maximum (18) before being caught and rewritten to the tokens `SCOPE_DRIFT`/`NONCONFORMANT`; had either landed on main as committed prose, this suite's AC3 non-zero control (still anchored to 18 as of #53) would need re-anchoring to 20 the moment that record was git-tracked -- confirmed the record did NOT land: `git show 055038e:.pipeline/53/status.json` does not exist (`.pipeline/` is gitignored except the `!.pipeline/*/status.json` negation, and this repo's own convention only commits per-phase CHECKPOINTS during an in-progress run, not the final archived state), so the corpus maximum remains 18 as of 055038e. RESOLUTION, closing the KNOWN OPEN GAP this entry carried since #34/#42: #53 widened BOTH Lane-1 drift derivations (test-voice-lint.sh, test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh) from the strict quoting-form regex (25 concrete literals) to a wide pattern matching every quoting form pipeline.md's writer uses (26 concrete literals, including '0-setup'), and DECLARED '0-setup' in voice-lint.mjs's NON_VOICE_PHASES and in gate-phase-entry.mjs's new fifth partition cell PRELUDE, so a run parked at 0-setup is no longer silently unaudited. The count-based vacuity floor this entry used to warn about ('>=20 is too loose to notice a single missing member') was itself replaced: #53 pins the exact 26-member sorted LABEL SET in both Lane-1 suites rather than a floor, per the #33 shape-ratchet precedent, so a future single-member narrowing reddens by name rather than by a floor miss. THE THREE-POPULATION FACT THIS ENTRY WARNED ABOUT IS NOW A DELIBERATE TWO-POPULATION FACT, NOT AN ACCIDENT: Lane 1's two suites now derive the SAME 26-literal set (0-setup included, halted-error excluded, since pipeline.md never writes it); Lane 2 (this suite, test-status-schema-contract.sh) derives its OWN 27-member ASSERTED set, which equals Lane 1's 26 PLUS halted-error, added by a stated rule specific to this suite (gate-phase-entry.mjs blesses halted-error by name even though pipeline.md never writes it). #53's spec explicitly refused (HANDOFF C, routed to a follow-up issue) a shared-derivation-helper fix that would collapse Lane 1 and Lane 2 onto one population, because such a helper could only safely return the raw pipeline.md EXTRACTION -- never an asserted set -- or it would silently delete halted-error from this suite. #53 named this suite (Lane 2) and tests/test-telemetry-exit-attribution.sh (Lane 2/3) as UNCHANGED CONSUMERS and verified the diff touches neither (`git diff --name-only 13e40e9...HEAD` at #53's reviewed commit names 6 files, none in Lane 2/3); re-confirm with the same command against 055038e if revisiting this. MEASURED RUN COST for #34, retained as a comparison baseline for future runs of similar shape: review_rounds=1, single four-role panel (BA/Dev/QA/SecOps), one nit round, one post-CI fix; suite assertion total, all measured on macOS Darwin 25.5.0 per #47's platform-carries-the-count rule: 1989 pre-change -> 2056 at the reviewed commit d8686bc (33 suites) -> 2063 after the nit round (+7) -> 2071 final on main at 0d0b8d5. Contrast: #39 (a related phase-vocabulary-rot issue) took seven review rounds; #53 (this closure) took two Phase 2 rounds plus one Phase 4 panel round, landing at 34 suites / 2629 assertions / 0 failed on main at 055038e.
